answers.answer: To replace part of a message, use {text.replace} with the text first, then the text to find, then the replacement. The example {text.replace:a-b|-| + } gives a + b. {text.replace.first} changes only the first match and {text.replace.icase} ignores letter case. To pluralize by a count, use {text.plural:count|singular|plural} (for example {text.plural:3|sub|subs} gives subs). {text.plural.count} gives the number together with the word, and {text.plural.auto:count|word} builds the plural form itself. Separate the inputs with a pipe after the colon, and nest {args} to use the words after a command.
answers.quote: Replaces every match of a text with another text

answers.answer: You need a template field that accepts the helper, as listed in the Use in column. For a pipeline you also need a trigger that supplies the message or event. For viewer-written text, the Viewer Templates setting and permissions also apply. The syntax comes first on the page: the input goes after a colon and a pipe separates the inputs.
answers.quote: A pipeline still needs a trigger that supplies the relevant person, message, or event; event-specific helpers need that event.

answers.answer: On success, the reply shows the transformed value, matching the Example column. On failure, the helper text itself stays in the reply. That happens with the wrong number of inputs, a count out of range, a position below 1, or an empty text to find in {text.replace}.
answers.quote: A helper that cannot use its input stays in the reply as written.

answers.answer: For the replace, {text.replace:message|find|replacement} changes every match and matches letter case exactly. {text.replace.first} changes only the first match and {text.replace.icase} ignores case. An empty text to find leaves the helper unchanged in the reply. For the plural, {text.plural:count|singular|plural} gives the singular word for 1 or -1 and the plural word for any other whole number, negative numbers included. {text.plural.count} adds the number in front, and {text.plural.auto:count|word} forms the plural automatically. The count goes first in all three.
answers.quote: The singular word for 1 or -1, the plural word for any other whole number

answers.answer: No sentence states the input order for each helper. This costs a reread of every example before writing a template, but the page does tell the reader to follow the examples.
answers.quote: Some take a number first, as in {text.first:3|hello}, so follow the order in each example.
